newsitem.title: USA: Total idles refinery as new capacity comes on line.
newsitem.headline: Total idles refinery as new capacity comes on line.

text.p: Total Petroleum Inc's idling of its Arkansas City, Kansas refinery is unlikely to affect Midwest product supplies as new regional capacity is seen compensating for loss of output, refiners said.

A steady stream of new capacity brought on line at Midwest refineries in recent years will displace the 58,000 barrel per day output lost as Total converts its crude oil refinery to a terminal and blending facility.
"I don't think it has a major impact on the market because of the Farmland increase," Merrill Lynch energy broker Dee Dee Finley said of Total's decision to trim its crude production.

Farmland Industries Inc is in the midst of a two-year project to increase output at its Coffeyville, Kansas refinery and lower refining costs to compete with shipments into the Group Three market from the Gulf Coast.

The expansion will boost capacity at the refinery to 125,000 barrels per day from the 68,600 barrels per day rated capacity two years ago and the current 95,000 barrel per day capacity, refinery general manager Coleman Ferguson said.
"We will get to the 125,000 barrels per day as we continue our debottlenecking," Ferguson said.

While Farmland embarked on a major expansion -- adding a crude still, reformer and sulphur unit while debottlenecking crude units -- capacity also has been creeping higher at other refineries in the region.
Texaco's El Dorado, Kansas refinery, for example, is now rated at 105,000 barrels per day, up from 94,600 barrels, following addition of a hydrotreater and other upgrades.
And Mobil Corp's Joliet, Illinois refinery is now rated at 200,000 barrel throughput, up from 188,000 barrels per day.
Total will continue to supply its Midwest branded gasoline stations with output from a 68,000 barrel per day refinery in Ardmore, Okla., a refinery spokeswoman said.
